evals.prompt: Lint the marketing copy under apps/web/app/(marketing) with slop-cop and tell me what it would cost before you run it.
evals.expected_output: Runs `slop-cop lint apps/web/app/(marketing) --dry-run` first, quotes the unit count, request count and estimated cost, then runs the lint without asking again, and summarises act and review findings separately with units, cost and the scorecard delta by category.
assertions: Runs a --dry-run before any live run
Quotes the estimated request count and cost from the dry run
Runs the live lint without a further confirmation prompt
Reports act and review findings separately and quotes the cost line

evals.prompt: slop-cop reported [MAJOR?] copywriting-vague-error (p=0.52) on the checkout error string. Is that a blocker?
evals.expected_output: Explains that MAJOR is the severity if real and the ? marks the review band, so the run did not fail on it; recommends reading the string and either fixing it or adding it to the corpus with the right label, and does not downgrade the severity because the probability is middling.
assertions: Does not lower the severity to express uncertainty
Suggests a corpus label or a fix rather than editing the threshold by hand

evals.prompt: Fix every typography-straight-quotes finding in docs/, including the ones inside code fences.
evals.expected_output: Points out that slop-cop does not report straight quotes inside code fences or inline code because they are correct there, runs --fix (or edits only the reported prose units), shows the diff, leaves code untouched, and re-runs the lint on the changed files.
assertions: Refuses to curl quotes inside code
Uses the deterministic fix or edits only reported prose units
Re-runs the lint on the changed files and reports the result
